title: Directional token buckets + streaming latency surcharge experiment
creator: Rina Shah
description: Run an experiment to validate asymmetric input/output token pricing and a streaming latency surcharge for long-lived streams, and capture requirements for enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) language around pricing minimums and billing clarity.
background: Sales and legal teams have reported repeated negotiation friction on enterprise deals where customers ask for clear separation of ingress vs egress charges and predictable behavior for streaming endpoints. Current hosted per-token pricing is symmetric and does not surface latency-related overhead on long streams. We believe introducing directional token buckets (cheaper input, higher-cost output) plus a small per-second streaming latency surcharge beyond a threshold could better reflect our cost profile and unlock clearer contract language for enterprise customers.
proposal: Define directional token rates: 0.8x for input tokens, 1.2x for output tokens for the experiment cohort
Add streaming latency surcharge: $0.0005 / second for active streams that exceed 30 seconds of continuous streaming (apply to streaming endpoints only)
Introduce per-request minimum: requests consuming < 10 tokens billed as 10 tokens equivalent to prevent noise in economics
Create an opt-in experiment flag for customers with > $2k/month spend and a controlled sample of self-serve accounts
Surface directional pricing and surcharge in billing UI and in the enterprise SQ language samples for Sales/Legal
metrics: Change in gross margin per 1M tokens processed (baseline vs experiment)
Delta in average invoice variance for enterprise deals referencing streaming (>30s)
Adoption rate of opt-in cohort and conversion lift for enterprise proposals with updated SQ language
Number of support tickets citing billing confusion (expected decrease)
Latency/SLO impact on requests (should be nil)
rollout_plan: Week 0: final PRD, legal approves sample SQ language, engineering scoping complete
Week 1-2: implement billing hooks and experiment flagging; add display fields in Console billing preview
Week 3: internal dry run using synthetic workloads and cost-model simulation
Week 4-8: launch opt-in cohort (enterprise invites + small self-serve subset), collect telemetry
Week 9: analyze results and run pricing sensitivity sim for broader rollout decision
